traceability.notes:
Story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING specifies cross-rule conventions for clear, actionable error messages (including placeholders, context fields, suggestions, and severity) across the core traceability rules. The current implementation: - Defines specific, templated messages in meta.messages for all relevant rules (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) that match the patterns described in the story. - Wires those templates through shared helpers (coreReportMissing/coreReportMethod, annotation-checker, branch-annotation-helpers, valid-annotation-format-validators/options, valid-story-reference-helpers, valid-req-reference-helpers) so ESLint reports include precise locations and rich data (functionName, missing, details, path, reqId, storyPath). - Provides ESLint suggestions and/or autofixes where appropriate, especially for missing @story and @req annotations, and documents these behaviors. - Implements and tests a severity policy that treats missing annotations and unresolved references as errors while treating pure format issues as warnings, exactly as specified. - Includes dedicated tests that are explicitly annotated with @supports for this story and its REQ-ERROR-* requirement IDs, all of which currently pass.
No discrepancies were found between the story’s acceptance criteria and the current implementation/test suite, so this story is fully implemented and verified.
